title: Magneto-optical signal from $\mathrm{Co_2Mn}$-based Heusler thin films in MOKE and BLS
authors: Anna Maria Friedel, Nicolas Fermon, Tobias Böttcher, Sébastien Petit-Watelot, Stéphane Andrieu, Philipp Pirro
abstract: $\mathrm{Co_2Mn}$-based Heusler compounds offer a versatile, composition-tunable platform for magnonics and spintronics. Among them, the half-metallic $\mathrm{Co_2MnSi}$ is of particular interest for magnonics owing to its ultralow Gilbert damping, yet its weak magneto-optical response in the visible challenges optical probing such as Brillouin light scattering (BLS). We study the magneto-optical response of epitaxial $\mathrm{Co_2Mn}X$ films ($X = \{\mathrm{Al}_x\mathrm{Si}_{1-x}, \mathrm{Ga}_x\mathrm{Ge}_{1-x}, \mathrm{Sn}\}$) by magneto-optical Kerr effect (MOKE) spectroscopy and BLS. Angle-resolved MOKE resolves a significant, wavelength-dependent quadratic MOKE (QMOKE) only for $\mathrm{Co_2MnSi}$, whereas $\mathrm{Co_2MnAl}$, $\mathrm{Co_2MnGa}$ and $\mathrm{Co_2MnSn}$ respond dominantly linearly. Comparing BLS intensities of thermal magnons at two wavelengths, $\mathrm{Co_2MnSi}$ gives the weakest signal at $532\,\mathrm{nm}$ yet among the strongest at $457\,\mathrm{nm}$, tracking the spectral dependence of its Kerr angle. These results emphasise the relation between the two magneto-optical techniques, guiding the choice of probing wavelength for $\mathrm{Co_2Mn}$-based Heusler compounds.
summary: This work investigates the magneto-optical properties of $\mathrm{Co_2Mn}$-based Heusler thin films using both MOKE and BLS. The key finding is that the distinct spectral behavior observed in MOKE (especially quadratic contributions) directly correlates with the intensity variations seen in BLS measurements. This establishes a powerful experimental methodology for selecting optimal wavelengths when probing magnetic excitations.
main_problem: To investigate the magneto-optical response of $\mathrm{Co_2Mn}$-based Heusler thin films using both Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect (MOKE) and Brillouin Light Scattering (BLS).
main_result: The study establishes a direct experimental link between MOKE spectroscopy and BLS measurements, showing that the spectral dependence observed in one technique can guide the optimal probing wavelength for the other.
method: Measurements involve angle-resolved MOKE spectroscopy to separate linear and quadratic magneto-optical contributions, complemented by BLS intensity measurements of thermal magnons at multiple wavelengths.
model_or_system: The physical system is epitaxial $\mathrm{Co_2MnX}$ Heusler thin films ($\mathrm{X} = \{\mathrm{Al}_x\mathrm{Si}_{1-x}, \mathrm{Ga}_x\mathrm{Ge}_{1-x}, \mathrm{Sn}\}$), which are studied for their spintronic and magnonic properties.
key_observables: Linear MOKE ($	heta_{	ext{linMOKE}}$), Quadratic MOKE ($	heta_{	ext{QMOKE}}$), BLS intensity of thermal magnons, and the spectral dependence of these signals across different wavelengths.
important_parameters: Wavelengths used for probing (e.g., $457\,\mathrm{nm}$ vs. $532\,\mathrm{nm}$); material composition ($\mathrm{Co_2MnX}$).
main_assumptions: The simple symmetry-based separation approach used in MOKE cannot fully distinguish between all possible symmetries of the quadratic magneto-optical contributions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the MOKE setup, the method for separating hysteresis loops into odd (linear) and even (quadratic) components, and comparisons of BLS intensities at different wavelengths.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares MOKE results across various $\mathrm{Co_2MnX}$ films to identify characteristic responses ($\mathrm{Co_2MnSi}$ showing strong QMOKE vs. others being linear). It then correlates these findings with wavelength-dependent BLS measurements, culminating in the conclusion that MOKE guides BLS probing.
why_interesting: While primarily experimental condensed matter physics, the detailed study of spin wave dynamics and magneto-optical response provides fundamental insights into magnetic order parameters and their coupling to optical probes, which is relevant for understanding quantum magnetodynamics.
